# Parley v0.1.52

The worktree manager, built to the design agreed on 13 September 2026.

## The Worktrees window

**Tools › Worktrees…** opens a window that needs no pane or workspace. Its
left column lists every repository Parley knows: the repositories of pane
folders, attached, favourite and recent folders, worktree records, and any
folder you add with **Add Repository…**, which is remembered in
`worktree-repositories.json` until you **Forget** it. Only a repository
known solely from your addition can be forgotten; the others come back on
their own. A repository whose folder is gone stays listed and marked
missing.

Select a repository and every worktree Git registers is a row: the primary
first and never removable, then each linked tree as a board row with its
state, owner, base, HEAD, changed paths and commits ahead of and behind the
primary. Git's registry is the list; Parley's record, when there is one,
adds base, team and requester. A tree Parley holds no record for reads
**Not recorded**; a registration whose folder is gone reads **Stale**.
Facts are read for the selected repository only, while the window is on
screen, and are never stored. **Workspace › Open Worktree…** now opens this
window on the active pane's repository, as does the pane notice's worktree
action.

## Actions on any tree

Every linked row offers **Open**, **Integrate…**, **Finish…** and
**Remove…**, whether or not Parley created the tree. Finish and Remove
write Parley's record for an unrecorded tree on the way in, so Track
Existing is gone as a step. Integrate on an unrecorded tree uses the
registry's branch and refuses a detached HEAD. Removal identity and every
refusal are unchanged from v0.1.51.

A **Stale** row offers **Prune…**. Git has no per-entry prune, so the
preview lists every prunable entry of the repository and you acknowledge
that list; one `git worktree prune` runs, nothing on disk or in branches
changes, and Parley clears its records for the forgotten entries.

**Delete Branch…** is offered after a successful removal and after a
prune, for the branches those trees held: one `git branch -d` per branch
after a preview that says whether its commit is contained in the primary
checkout and whether any worktree entry, stale or not, still holds it. Git
refuses an unmerged or held branch in its own words. Parley never uses
`-D`. Git counts a prunable entry as still holding its branch, which is why
the branch step follows the prune rather than sitting on the stale row.

## Remove integrated…

The window's one bulk action. It builds a single preview over every tree
of the selected repository that reads Integrated, from fresh checks: each
passing tree with what was verified and every ignored entry that would go
with it, each skipped tree with the refusal that keeps it. Confirming
removes the passing trees one `git worktree remove` at a time, without
`--force`, and stops at the first outcome that is not a confirmed removal.
The branches of the removed trees are offered afterwards, one confirmation
each. Nothing runs across repositories at once.

## Gone

The Open Worktree… sheet, its two lists, the Managed by Parley section,
Track Existing and the Finish & Cleanup tab. Finish… on a row opens the
same four-step inspector as a sheet on the window.

## Also fixed

A freshly created or tracked tree read "Not read yet" until the browser
was reopened, because those paths refreshed facts only for trees with panes
inside.

## Compatibility

Agent protocol unchanged at 32. No pane needs a restart. New file:
`worktree-repositories.json` (added folders only, mode 0600).

Validated: 359 native checks (six new: repository merge and store, registry
rows, prune, branch deletion, the bulk plan), 53 Node tests, public scan,
platform scan and build. Hand-verified in the development app: the window
opened from Tools with no repository selected by a pane, listed six
repositories with their sources, removed an unrecorded tree and then its
branch, pruned a stale entry and then its branch, refused a held branch,
and removed two integrated trees while skipping a dirty one.

Unnotarized test beta: ad-hoc signed without the hardened runtime, not
notarized, no automatic updates. Install only from the expected GitLab
release after checking SHA256SUMS.
